decision.observation: 10 mph, gear 1, timer 22:59.733, three blue dots. The camera has rotated again: the gravel now runs up the RIGHT of the frame, and the car sits off-road on grass to its left among pines, nose angled up-frame toward the road's left edge and white posts.
decision.hypothesis: The W+D hold at 12 mph did not zero the car but it did carry it off the left edge of the road, so 12 mph steering is survivable yet imprecise. At 10 mph the precedent that most resembles this state is a W+A rejoin onto gravel from 10 mph off-road, so one short W+A beat should rotate it back onto the track.
decision.memory: Corrected cost model: 12 mph steer is not an instant kill; it drifts the car off the far edge instead. The practical rule stays: keep bends at ~10 mph where rejoins have been reliable.
